skill.name: gws-drive
skill.description: Manage Google Drive files, folders, shared drives, comments, permissions, revisions, and notifications through the gws CLI.
skill.summary: Use the gws CLI to inspect and manage Google Drive resources.
skill.author: googleworkspace

security_audit.summary: All 111 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, documentation links, relative sibling references, and Drive API method descriptions. No prompt injection or malicious behavior appears, but consequential Drive mutations need explicit confirmation.

remediation.issue: Consequential approval, deletion, update, and permission methods lack confirmation guidance in this file.
remediation.suggestion: Require a preview and explicit user confirmation before changing access, deleting content, resolving proposals, or replacing file data.

remediation.issue: Authentication and security rules depend on a sibling skill referenced at runtime.
remediation.suggestion: Package the shared guidance with this skill and stop execution when it cannot be loaded.

semantic_findings.title: Consequential Drive Operations Need Confirmation
semantic_findings.description: The skill lists approval, deletion, file update, permission change, and revision deletion methods without local confirmation requirements. Broad requests could cause data loss or access changes.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The methods are explicitly documented at the cited lines. Confidence is slightly reduced because line 16 delegates security rules to a sibling skill.

content.value_statement: Google Drive administration often requires many separate API operations. This skill guides Claude and Codex through supported gws commands for files, sharing, comments, revisions, and notifications.
actual_capabilities: List, inspect, copy, create, update, download, and export Drive files.
Create, inspect, hide, restore, and update shared drives.
Create, list, update, and delete comments and replies.
Create, inspect, update, and delete file or shared drive permissions.
Inspect file revisions and delete eligible binary file revisions.
Watch file or Drive changes and stop notification channels.
limitations: Requires an authenticated gws CLI with suitable Google Workspace scopes.
Google account permissions and administrator policies limit every operation.
Workspace exports are limited to 10 MB, and other Drive API limits still apply.
Authentication guidance and upload behavior are delegated to sibling skills.

use_cases.title: Organize Team Files
use_cases.description: Find files, inspect metadata, create folders, and update selected items in a team workspace.

use_cases.title: Review Sharing Access
use_cases.description: List permissions and pending access proposals before applying approved sharing changes.

use_cases.title: Automate Content Workflows
use_cases.description: Monitor Drive changes, export documents, and manage comments for connected business processes.

prompt_templates.title: Find Recent Files
prompt_templates.prompt: List non-trashed files modified after [date]. Return each name, type, owner, modified time, and file ID.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect a Shared Drive
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect shared drive [drive ID]. Summarize its metadata and list matching files using query [query]. Do not change anything.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Permission Changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Review permissions for [file ID]. Propose changes for [people or groups], explain access impact, and wait for confirmation before applying them.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Change Monitor
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect the Drive change methods, obtain the required page token, and plan notifications for [scope]. Confirm channel settings before creating the watch.

output_examples.input: List non-trashed PDF files modified this week in the Finance folder.
output: Quarterly Forecast.pdf, modified August 4, owned by Finance Operations.
Expense Policy.pdf, modified August 2, owned by Workplace Services.
Two matching files found. No Drive content was changed.

output_examples.input: Review who can edit the project brief and suggest least-privilege changes.
output_examples.output: The review found three editors and one domain-wide viewer. It recommends retaining project leads and removing obsolete access after confirmation.

output_examples.input: Export the presentation as a PDF and summarize the result.
output_examples.output: The presentation was exported as a PDF within the documented size limit. The response includes the destination and exported file size.

best_practices: Inspect each method schema before building parameters or request data.
Use narrow fields and search queries to reduce returned Drive data.
Preview consequential changes and obtain explicit confirmation before execution.
anti_patterns: Do not list every file when a narrow query can answer the request.
Do not delete revisions, comments, permissions, or files without explicit confirmation.
Do not assume the authenticated account can access every shared drive.

faq.question: What does this skill require?
faq.answer: It requires the gws CLI, Google authentication, suitable scopes, and access to the relevant Drive resources.

faq.question: Can it upload local files?
faq.answer: The skill references a separate upload helper that handles file uploads and metadata.

faq.question: Can it manage shared drives?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents creating, listing, inspecting, hiding, restoring, and updating shared drives.

faq.question: Can it change file permissions?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports permission creation, inspection, updates, and deletion when the authenticated user is authorized.

faq.question: Does it support downloads and exports?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents file downloads and Workspace document exports, including the 10 MB export limit.

faq.question: How should destructive operations be handled?
faq.answer: Review the target and expected impact, then obtain explicit user confirmation before any deletion or access change.
